title: Federated Learning of Explainable AI(FedXAI) for deep learning-based intrusion detection in IoT networks
researchArea: Cybersecurity, Federated Learning, Explainable AI, IoT Intrusion Detection Systems
problem: Integrating Explainable AI into Federated Learning for IoT intrusion detection without violating client data privacy, as traditional post-hoc XAI methods like SHAP require central access to client raw data or background baselines to interpret the global model.
motivation: Security Operation Center analysts struggle to trust black-box Deep Learning models in intrusion detection systems without interpretability. Existing federated learning solutions ensure privacy during training but lack privacy-preserving explainability mechanisms for the server-side global model.
noveltyAndContributions: Proposed the FedXAI framework combining LSTM-based horizontal federated learning with privacy-preserving SHAP explanations for IoT intrusion detection.
Introduced a Secure Multiparty Computation Secret Sharing protocol to securely aggregate client-side SHAP values into global server explanations without sharing raw client data.
Rigorously evaluated local post-hoc explanations (SHAP, LIME, IG) across participating clients using four quantitative metrics: High Faithfulness, Monotonicity, Low Complexity, and Max Sensitivity.
Achieved state-of-the-art detection performance across binary, botnet-type, and attack-type classification tasks on the N-BaIoT dataset.
methodology: Long Short-Term Memory neural network trained via Federated Averaging in Horizontal Federated Learning.
Min-Max feature scaling preprocessing standardizing data within range 0 to 1.
Secure aggregation of client SHAP attributions using a Secure Multiparty Computation Secret Sharing protocol.
Verification of securely aggregated client SHAP values against server global baseline using an element-wise divergence matrix.
Post-hoc local explanations for client models evaluated using LIME, Integrated Gradients, and SHAP.
keyAssumptions: Clients share identical feature and label space in a Horizontal Federated Learning setting.
Participating clients execute the Secure Multiparty Computation Secret Sharing protocol for secure SHAP value aggregation.
Data is partitioned in an independent and identically distributed setting across IoT edge devices for baseline analysis.
datasets: N-BaIoT dataset containing 115 network traffic statistical features from 9 IoT devices infected by Mirai and Gafgyt botnets.
partition: 80:20 train and validation split on local client data
Independent and identically distributed data distribution across participating IoT client devices
numClients: 9 IoT device clients for binary classification (Doorbell1, BabyMonitor, SecurityCam1, SecurityCam2, Thermostat, SecurityCam3, SecurityCam4, Doorbell2, Webcam)
7 IoT device clients for multiclass botnet-type and attack-type detection (excluding Doorbell2 and Webcam due to missing Mirai botnet traffic)
experimentalSetup: AMD Threadripper 3960X CPU (24 cores, 48 threads), 128 GB RAM, NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU (24 GB VRAM), Ubuntu 20.04 LTS HPC cluster node using Slurm.
Python 3.9, Flower federated learning framework with PyTorch.
Hyperparameters: Adam optimizer with learning rate 0.001, ReLU activation function.
Batch size: 256 for binary and botnet-type classification, 512 for attack-type classification.
Local epochs: 50 for binary, 100 for botnet-type, 200 for attack-type classification.
Communication rounds: 10 for binary, 50 for botnet-type, 2000 for attack-type classification.
50 percent random client selection per round during training, 100 percent participation in evaluation.
baselines: MLP (Rey et al.) with Mini-Batch Multi-Epoch aggregation
CNN (Do et al.) with Mini-Batch aggregation
LSTM (Parra et al.) distributed learning model
Server-side SHAP explanations generated with direct access to client training and testing data
flAlgorithms: Federated Averaging in Horizontal Federated Learning
xaiEvaluation: Quantitative evaluation of local post-hoc explanations across 2000 test data points per client using four metrics: High Faithfulness correlation, Monotonicity percentage, Low Complexity entropy, and Max Sensitivity (radius r=0.1).
metrics: Divergence matrix difference between server-side and client-side explanations
results: The FedAvg LSTM model achieved 99.90% accuracy (99.99% F1-score) for binary malware detection, 99.28% accuracy (99.54% F1-score) for botnet-type detection, and 94.89% accuracy (94.50% F1-score) for attack-type detection. Securely aggregated client SHAP explanations closely approximated full-access server explanations with divergence values near zero. SHAP outperformed LIME and IG in faithfulness, lower complexity, monotonicity, and stability.
failureConditions: Minor divergence between client-aggregated and server global explanations observed for specific features such as MI_dir_L0.1_weight and H_L0.1_weight under local sample variations.
Performance fluctuations during early communication rounds for specific heterogeneous IoT devices like Thermostat and SecurityCam4.
costEvaluation: Computing SHAP values via DeepExplainer on local clients is computationally expensive due to game-theoretic Shapley value estimations. SMPC secret sharing aggregation is lightweight and introduces minimal communication overhead during federated rounds. Evaluating Max Sensitivity is computationally intensive due to neighborhood distance search.

limitations.text: High computational complexity of SHAP value calculation makes scaling to large numbers of IoT clients less feasible.
Experiments evaluated performance on independent and identically distributed data splits rather than realistic non-IID IoT data distributions.
SMPC aggregation remains vulnerable to inference attacks, adversarial manipulation of post-hoc explanations, explanation-based membership inference attacks, and federated model poisoning attacks.
Resource constraints of edge IoT devices (limited compute, memory, battery, bandwidth) make training deep networks energy-intensive and time-consuming.

futureWork: Explore synthetic data generation at the server to calculate global model explanations without relying on client SHAP aggregation.
Evaluate FedXAI under non-IID data distributions and heterogeneous IoT network topologies.
Integrate homomorphic encryption and differential privacy to defend against inference attacks and adversarial explanation manipulation.
Implement Byzantine-robust aggregation methods such as Krum, Trimmed Mean, and Median filtering against model poisoning.
Apply model pruning and adaptive client selection to optimize energy and resource consumption on edge devices.
relevance: Highly relevant for privacy-preserving cybersecurity, trustworthy explainable AI, IoT botnet detection, and quantitative XAI evaluation in federated learning architectures.
newIdeas: Privacy-preserving SMPC Secret Sharing aggregation of Shapley values from federated learning clients to explain server global models without raw data transfer.
Quantitative multi-metric benchmarking framework (Faithfulness, Monotonicity, Complexity, Sensitivity) for post-hoc XAI in federated security settings.
reviewStatus: Published in Computer Networks, Volume 270, Article 111479, Elsevier (2025).
